permitted_inputs: state (from Census lookup), only for rules with a stated geographic basis
optional user-reported context (fixed dropdown answers, labeled unverified)

geographic_scope.basis: Soil sampling guidance is general; sampling depth and timing should follow the user's state land-grant laboratory.

prerequisites.description: No soil test in the last 3 years

rules.trigger: Selected area is verified as corn or wheat in the CDL year.

content.action: Consider whether a current soil test is available before making nutrient or lime decisions for this area.
content.why: Extension guidance treats soil sampling as the starting point for fertility decisions; a test shows actual nutrient and pH levels rather than assumptions.

general_context.corn: Missouri Extension notes the best time to sample is when ground is idle; for spring-planted crops such as corn that is typically late fall or winter.
general_context.wheat: Missouri Extension notes the best time to sample is when ground is idle; for winter wheat that is typically summer, after harvest.

cost_effort.explanation: Sampling takes field time and a laboratory fee; it does not require new equipment.

limitations: FieldWise has no soil data for this area and does not know whether a recent soil test exists.
verify_before_acting: Whether a recent soil test already exists for this ground.
Your state laboratory's recommended sampling depth, timing and area per composite sample.

geographic_scope.basis: General extension guidance; suitability varies with soil drainage, slope and climate.

prerequisites.description: The area is currently managed with conventional tillage

rules.trigger: Selected area is verified as corn or wheat; current tillage is unknown, so the rule is presented conditionally.
rules.conditional_prefix: If this area is currently tilled:

content.action: Consider assessing whether reducing tillage intensity (for example, no-till or other residue-retaining systems) could fit this operation.
content.why: Keeping crop residue on the surface can reduce sheet and rill erosion; Penn State Extension reports that about 30% residue cover reduced this erosion roughly 70% compared with bare soil in rainfall-simulation studies.

general_context.corn: Penn State Extension notes no-till soils run cooler in spring, so corn may emerge and grow more slowly early in the season — described as a temporary effect.
general_context.wheat: Residue-retaining systems are commonly used in small-grain rotations; equipment and residue management needs differ by region.

cost_effort.explanation: May require planter or drill changes and new residue, weed and fertility management skills; suitability depends on soil drainage and slope.

limitations: The CDL does not show tillage practices; this area may already use reduced tillage.
verify_before_acting: Current tillage practice and residue cover.
Soil drainage and compaction on this ground.
Equipment needs and local experience — discuss suitability with a local agricultural adviser or extension office.

geographic_scope.basis: Applies only where a field is irrigated; irrigation status is not available from the CDL.

rules.trigger: Selected area is verified as corn or wheat; irrigation status is unknown, so the rule is presented conditionally.

content.action: Consider assessing whether soil-moisture monitoring or a soil water balance tool could help time irrigation.
content.why: Extension guidance describes using soil moisture sensors or water-balance tools to decide when to irrigate and to avoid refilling beyond field capacity, which can conserve water and energy.

general_context.corn: Thresholds for when to irrigate depend on soil type and crop stage; extension materials describe a management allowable depletion approach.
general_context.wheat: Thresholds for when to irrigate depend on soil type and crop stage; extension materials describe a management allowable depletion approach.

cost_effort.explanation: Requires sensors or a scheduling tool plus regular readings during the season; telemetry adds convenience but has practical drawbacks.

limitations: FieldWise cannot tell whether this area is irrigated or how it is currently scheduled.
No irrigation schedule or amount is provided.
verify_before_acting: Whether the area is irrigated at all.
Soil water-holding characteristics and your state extension's irrigation guidance.

geographic_scope.basis: General extension guidance; cited research is from humid eastern states.

prerequisites.description: Crop residue is removed after harvest

rules.trigger: Selected area is verified as corn or wheat.

content.action: Consider whether keeping crop residue on the soil surface could help conserve soil moisture in this system.
content.why: Penn State Extension describes surface residue as an insulating layer that conserves moisture, citing Kentucky research that found more evaporative water loss from tilled than from no-till soil before canopy closure.

general_context.corn: Corn produces substantial residue; how much is retained depends on harvest and tillage choices.
general_context.wheat: Wheat stubble left after harvest is one form of surface residue; retention depends on tillage and any residue removal.

cost_effort.explanation: Mostly a management change linked to tillage choices; effects depend on climate, soil and residue amount.

limitations: The CDL does not show residue levels or soil moisture for this area.
verify_before_acting: Whether residue is used for other purposes (e.g., baling or grazing).
Local experience with residue and planting conditions.

geographic_scope.basis: General SARE guidance; species and timing are region-specific.

prerequisites.description: The area does not already use cover crops

rules.trigger: Selected area is verified as corn or wheat; existing cover crop use is unknown, so the rule is presented conditionally.
rules.conditional_prefix: If cover crops are not already used here:

content.action: Consider assessing whether a cover crop could fit between cash crops in this rotation.
content.why: SARE describes cover crops as reducing wind and water erosion, adding organic matter, scavenging or supplying nitrogen, and helping suppress weeds — while noting they need planning and payback may take several years.

general_context.corn: Timing is often the main constraint after a full-season crop such as corn; seeding windows depend on harvest date and region.
general_context.wheat: Harvest of small grains such as wheat can leave a summer or fall window for a cover crop, depending on region and rainfall.

cost_effort.explanation: Involves seed, planting and termination work and new management decisions; SARE notes payback may take a few years depending on the goal.

limitations: Whether cover crops are already used here is unknown.
In dry regions, cover crop water use needs careful consideration.
verify_before_acting: Existing cover crop use and herbicide carryover restrictions.
Seeding and termination windows for your region.
Species suited to your climate — discuss with a local agricultural adviser.

geographic_scope.basis: Member states covered by the Midwest Cover Crops Council.

prerequisites.description: The selected point's state was resolved

rules.trigger: Selected area is verified as corn or wheat AND its state is one of the Midwest Cover Crops Council states.

content.action: Consider using the Midwest Cover Crops Council's selector tools to explore cover crop species suited to this state.
content.why: The Council shares regional cover crop knowledge and offers tools to help select cover crops for field crop rotations in its member states.

general_context.corn: Regional tools can narrow species and timing options before a conversation with a local adviser.
general_context.wheat: Regional tools can narrow species and timing options before a conversation with a local adviser.

cost_effort.explanation: An online tool; the effort is the time to review options.

limitations: Tool output is general guidance for the state or region, not a field-specific prescription.
verify_before_acting: Local seed availability and termination plans.
Fit with your cash crop rotation.

geographic_scope.basis: General SARE guidance on diversified rotations.

rules.trigger: Selected area is verified as corn or wheat; rotation history is not available from a single-year classification, so the rule is presented conditionally.
rules.conditional_prefix: Depending on this area's rotation history (not known from one year of data):

content.action: Consider discussing whether a more diverse rotation — for example, including a small grain or another crop — could suit this operation.
content.why: SARE resources describe diversified rotations and cover crops together as tools for soil organic matter, nutrient cycling and weed management.

general_context.corn: One published farm profile (Indiana) describes growing winter wheat before corn with a cover crop mix after wheat harvest.
general_context.wheat: Small grains such as wheat are a common way rotations are diversified; the following crop choice depends on region and markets.

cost_effort.explanation: Depends on markets, equipment, storage and local agronomy; FieldWise has no information about these.

limitations: A single year of CDL data does not reveal the rotation history.
No market or profitability assessment is made.
verify_before_acting: Market access for any added crop.
Discuss suitability with a local agricultural adviser.
